Disseminated sclerosis denotes immune-mediated CNS demyelination; associated narcolepsy is also neurologic.
Carcinoma originates in laryngeal epithelium; the larynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Familial azotemia is an inherited abnormality of renal urea handling; azotemia alone does not establish damage to other organs.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are common across chromosome 1 deletion syndromes; other organ abnormalities depend on the deleted region.
Adenocarcinoma originates in the ethmoid sinus, part of the upper respiratory tract.
Defining mandibulofacial dysostosis, external/middle-ear malformations with hearing loss (~90%), and eyelid colobomas (~65%); cleft palate occurs in only 25%.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; dental abnormalities occur in 30-79%, hypotonia in 30-79% and pes planus in 2/4. Ocular and cardiac malformations are occasional.
CMV infection is usually asymptomatic; retinitis, gastrointestinal disease and pneumonia affect selected subgroups and are separately defined diseases.
Benign basal-cell epithelial neoplasm, interpreted as cutaneous; the supplied definition does not specify an anatomical site.
Inherited tendency to form excessive fibrotic scars in the skin.
Rhabdomyosarcoma originates in the orbit; myoblastic differentiation does not establish a separate skeletal-muscle disorder.
Inherited immunodeficiency with pathological lymphocyte proliferation and dysregulation; hepatitis, lymphoma and hemophagocytic syndromes are variable complications.

Hyperplasia directly affects urinary tract urothelium; the renal axis includes the collecting urinary tract.
Extreme insulin resistance; cardiomyopathy 3/3, cholestatic dysfunction 3/3, developmental disability 30-79%. Frequent skin/lipoatrophy and muscle changes omitted by cap.
Mucinous cystic neoplasm originates in extrahepatic bile ducts, included in the hepatic axis.
Permanent laryngeal paralysis and intellectual disability define the syndrome; bronchiectasis is also pulmonary and reported as obligate.
VZV reactivation causes dermatitis specifically involving the eyelid, covered by both ocular and skin axes; nerve latency alone does not establish neurologic damage.
Hepatic glycogen phosphorylase deficiency with hepatomegaly and transaminase elevation; osteopenia/osteoporosis occurs in 30-79%. Renal and cardiac damage is very rare.
Progressive pectorodorsal muscular dystrophy directly degenerates skeletal muscle; neuromuscular classification alone does not establish nerve damage.
Defective respiratory mucociliary clearance defines PCD; chronic middle-ear inflammation occurs in 30-79%. Situs reversal alone causes no cardiovascular damage.
Intellectual disability defines the syndrome; dental abnormalities including incisor microdontia occur in 80-99%. Macroorchidism is outside the axes.
Congenital nail dysplasia defines the disorder; abnormal finger phalanges and partial distal-phalanx duplication occur in 30-79%.
Rapid loss of respiratory function defines the condition; cardiovascular shock is a possible separate complication, not established common direct involvement.
